title: Linguistic collaborations
description: The Laboratory of Modern Languages collaborates with various services at Università della Svizzera italiana (USI) to support the study of Italian, French, German, and English.

items.title: Assessment test for languages - Outgoing USI students
items.html:
The LLM Laboratory of Modern Languages collaborates with the International Relations and Mobility Service to offer USI students the opportunity to take a language assessment test (Italian, French, German or English), assessing their language skills through a written and an oral test.

The assessment costs CHF 200 and enables students to obtain a confirmation letter indicating their level, based on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), for each part of the test, as well as an overall assessment.

Language assessment test – Academic year 2026–2027

The Laboratory of Modern Languages’ language assessment test, available for Italian, French, German and English, will take place on:

  • Friday, 27 November 2026

To register for the assessment, please complete the following online form: [link to be published by mid-October]

Following the results of the internal language assessment, the Laboratory of Modern Languages will issue a signed letter confirming the student’s language proficiency level, based on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).

Important information

The internal language assessment is intended to provide evidence of a student’s level of language proficiency in specific circumstances. Before registering, students are therefore advised to read the following information carefully:

  • The assessment does not replace an official language examination taken during an examination session at USI or at a recognised examination centre and should not be considered an alternative to such certification.

  • Not all universities accept a letter confirming a student’s language level issued by their home university. Where possible, students are therefore always advised to obtain an official, internationally recognised language certificate. For further information on official certifications for the four languages, please consult the dedicated pages: Italian, French, German, English.

  • Before registering for the assessment, students should check the requirements of their host university and make sure that the letter issued by the Laboratory of Modern Languages will be accepted. If, after taking the assessment, a student decides to apply to a university that does not recognise this form of evidence, they may be required to take an additional test or provide a certificate that meets the university’s requirements.

items.title: ITERSS-funded courses
items.html:
The ITERSS Inclusive Tertiary Education for Refugees in Southern Switzerland is an initiative launched through the collaboration between USI’s International Relations and Study Abroad Service and SUPSI’s International Office, with the aim of promoting equitable access to higher education for people with a refugee background.

Building on the collaboration established through the InclUSIone programme, the Laboratory of Modern Languages contributes to the ITERSS project by offering upper-intermediate language courses. These courses enable applicants to meet the language proficiency requirement for admission to the degree programmes offered by the two universities.

For further information, please visit the dedicated website.
Contacts: Mariaelena Biliato and Maurizia Ruinelli

items.title: Courses dedicated to USI staff
items.html:
Since the 2023–2024 academic year, the Human Resources Service, as part of the Training and Development programme, has been collaborating with the Laboratory of Modern Languages to organise and promote English language courses for administrative staff.
Over the years, the range of courses has gradually expanded to include levels from beginner to upper-intermediate, meeting the diverse learning needs of participants.

items.title: Conversation workshops for students
items.html:
The collaboration with the Student Corporation stems from a shared commitment to fostering interaction and exchange among people from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds within the university community.

One of the initiatives developed in collaboration with the Student Corporation is the "Conversation workshops for students" project, which is offered every year during the spring semester. The workshops are held in Italian, French, English and German, providing an informal setting in which participants can develop their language skills through conversation.

Each year, the Laboratory of Modern Languages publishes a call for applications to recruit volunteer workshop moderators. Applications are open to native speakers as well as to individuals who have achieved C2-level proficiency in the language of the workshop they wish to moderate.

The workshops take place in small groups and consist of two one-hour meetings per month, for a total of five hours. Volunteering as a moderator is an excellent opportunity to put language skills into practice, gain experience in facilitating group discussions, meet people from different cultural backgrounds and contribute actively to university life by promoting linguistic and intercultural exchange. At the end of the project, the LLM awards all selected volunteers a certificate of collaboration in recognition of their contribution to the initiative.

Over the past few years, Conversation Workshops have been offered in different languages and at a range of proficiency levels, depending on the availability of volunteer moderators.
